props.covers: The sync, run, and PR phases that move a game from upstream intake through autonomous work to review-ready publication.

text.insert: A game moves through sync, run, and PR workflows. Each phase occupies its own

workflow slot, may acquire the dispatch lease, and operates its own queue workers without creating a second source of game authority. HarnessState is the harness's per-game coordination record for revision, dispatch-lease holder, queued requests, and blockers.

HarnessState
  -> sync workflow slot
       -> baseline intake and staged reconciliation
  -> run workflow slot
       -> epoch queue and epoch workers
  -> PR workflow slot
       -> review queue and review agents

Dispatch lease
  -> held by at most one active workflow
  -> transferred only through a durable handoff

The active workflow owns dispatch decisions and the checkout surfaces assigned to its phase. A queued or observed workflow may record intent, but it cannot dispatch workers or mutate protected state until it holds the lease.
Knowledge processing uses durable background jobs rather than a fourth game phase.
defines which knowledge work is background-safe and which work waits for sync staging and publication.
The end-to-end walk through these phases — registration and cycle open, the sync baseline, run epochs, the PR campaign, and the knowledge lane running alongside — lives in
. This index keeps the phase model and the per-workflow detail pages.
Each child workflow follows the same three-part shape: an overview of the phase, its durable state, and its detailed flows.
each open with the overview and link down from there.
